summary: Frontend-only validation of the new Mapa/Satélite toggle (MapBaseLayers) across all maps of Xaluca Tours. Tested on /juego, /cuando-viajar, /marruecos, /viajes/atlas_desierto/programa_4n_5d, /que-ver-en-Marruecos, in desktop (1920), tablet (768) and mobile (390). Toggle is present, default state is 'Mapa' (aria-pressed=true), clicking 'Satélite' loads Esri arcgisonline tiles and switches aria-pressed, clicking 'Mapa' returns CartoDB tiles. No console errors, no map pan/zoom on toggle click (propagation disabled), markers/polylines (12 SVG paths on TripRouteMap) persist after each switch. Each map has its own independent toggle (7 toggles on the trip detail page = 1 TripRouteMap + 6 DayRouteMaps). Responsive: toggle remains visible and legible at 390px (124x27px) and 768px (143x29px) without overlapping the top-right Xaluca logo (toggle is at bottom-right).
critical_code_review_comments: MapBaseLayers.jsx: 'satellite' state is local to each <MapBaseLayers/>, which is the intended per-map behaviour. Looks clean (~127 lines).

Esri labels overlay (Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places) renders on top of the imagery — fine for current Spanish/English/French use; consider attribution string in DOM is shown only once which is acceptable.
Toggle uses Spanish labels by default via LanguageContext fallback — English/French translations also available (LABELS dict).
Tile DOM remains in memory (Leaflet keeps both layers as separate <TileLayer> components when state toggles); this is React-Leaflet's standard behavior and not a leak.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mapa/Satélite toggle validated across 5 map-bearing pages with 4 variants (light, labeled, dark, light per-day). Esri tiles confirmed loading (≥24 tiles in the viewport on each switch). Marker/polyline persistence checked via SVG path count (stable at 12 on TripRouteMap before/during/after switch). Pan/zoom suppression verified via .leaflet-map-pane transform stability. No actions needed.
